title: Introduce tenant hibernation with egress taxonomy adjuster and circuit slew-rate controller
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds graceful tenant hibernation for extreme oversubscription scenarios; introduces an egress taxonomy adjuster to preferentially reduce cross-region egress; introduces a slew-rate controller on the circuit fuse to prevent rapid flip-flopping; includes telemetry and migration script.
description:
Context: During a recent regional surge incident we observed tenants with unexpected cross-region egress patterns causing egress-driven overload and rapid circuit flips during failovers. Small tenants throttled aggressively were still contributing to noisy KV evacuation and triggering stale circuit reopen attempts. This PR introduces a controlled 'tenant hibernation' mechanism coupled with an egress taxonomy adjuster and a circuit slew-rate controller to provide a graceful, observable way to remove noisy tenants from active serving while preserving SLOs for healthy tenants.

What I changed: 1) tenant hibernation controller: a short-lived lifecycle that marks tenants as HIBERNATED when their combined cost and egress weight exceeds the soft budget; hibernation preserves KV sticky entries and provides a timebound suspend window for the tenant's requests to drain; it is reversible and tier-aware. 2) egress taxonomy adjuster: classifies egress per-request into LOCAL, CROSS_REGION, and HIGH_BANDWIDTH buckets and adjusts admission/egress budget tokens to preferentially reduce CROSS_REGION egress before dropping LOCAL traffic. This helps keep regional capacity local during failovers. 3) circuit slew-rate controller: prevents the circuit fuse from toggling rapidly by enforcing a configurable min-open window and a programmable reopen-slew curve (linear backoff with jitter cap). 4) telemetry: new metrics and events (tenant_hibernate.enter, tenant_hibernate.exit, egress.adjustment, circuit.slew_applied) and dashboards added. 5) migration: a small config migration that populates default taxonomy weights and enables tenant hibernation opt-in for Dedicated customers.

Why this is different: Existing soft-degradation and eviction mechanisms target admission or priority queues. Tenant hibernation is an explicit tenant lifecycle state that preserves data locality and KV coherence while suspending acceptance of new requests; paired with egress classification it reduces cross-region thrash, and the slew controller addresses the oscillation vector we witnessed during the incident.

Tests and rollout: Unit tests for controller state transitions and egress classification added. Integration test harness simulates a regional egress storm and asserts that hibernated tenants do not cause KV re-evacs and that healthy tenants keep SLOs. Canary rollout: default off for hosted customers, opt-in for Dedicated; smoke canary in prod region us-east-1 with a 1% sample; automated rollback if 5xx rate increases by >0.5pp over baseline.

Related work: ENG-4982 tracks the wider egress taxonomy initiative; ENG-5021 is the incident follow-up with proposed controls. SUP-7214 is a support ticket for a customer impacted by egress-driven failover.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the controller state machine (controller/tenant_hibernate.go), the egress classifier rules (runtime/egress_taxonomy.go), and the circuit slew implementation (runtime/circuit_slew_controller.go). The migration script is under infra/migrations/2026-02-tenant-hibernate.sql and must be safe to run during rolling upgrades.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Overall looks good. Two concerns: a) migration - can we make the SQL idempotent for older clusters? b) the default taxonomy weights look aggressive; suggest conservative defaults that we can ramp.
Maya Chen (reply): Migration is idempotent - we use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT and a safe backfill; updated default weights to be 20% cross_region reduction instead of 40%.
Asha Patel: I'm worried about hibernation for latency-sensitive tenants. Can we expose a per-tenant opt-out and surface an audit event when hibernation is applied?
Maya Chen (reply): Added tenant-level opt-out flag and audit events (tenant_hibernate.audit). Also documented operator guidance in docs/operational/tenant-hibernate.md.
Oliver Nguyen: Tests look thorough. One nit: the circuit slew jitter cap currently uses a deterministic seed in tests; switched to mocked jitter for stability.
Maya Chen (reply): Fixed tests to mock jitter and added an integration scenario for KV-drain race reproduction.
